ai.description: This lizard reaches 45 cm, featuring a sandy-brown body with dark spots. It is distinguished by a flattened, heavily spined tail and enlarged, keeled scales on the hind limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Saara hardwickii* is its distinctively flattened, spade-like tail covered in whorls of large, sharp, spinose scales.
ai.habitat: The Indian Spiny-tailed Lizard inhabits arid and semi-arid regions, specifically favoring flat, hard-packed sandy plains with sparse xerophytic scrub vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Indian Spiny-tailed Lizard is primarily herbivorous, foraging for grasses and seeds during the heat of the day when it emerges from its burrow to bask in the sun.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Saara hardwickii* is oviparous, laying a single clutch of 6–15 eggs annually. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon period, typically from April to June.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Saara hardwickii* inhabits the arid and semi-arid regions of northwestern India, primarily across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and parts of Punjab, typically at low elevations.
